title: Looking Ahead
description: Membicarakan rencana, janji temu, keputusan, dan prediksi tentang masa depan. Kamu akan membandingkan will, be going to, dan present continuous, memakai future time clauses (when, as soon as, before, after, until), serta might/may untuk kemungkinan — dengan tema teknologi dan masa depan.
objectives: Memilih will, be going to, atau present continuous sesuai jenis rencana atau keputusan
Membuat prediksi berdasarkan opini (will) dan bukti saat ini (going to)
Menggunakan present simple setelah when, as soon as, before, after, dan until untuk masa depan
Menyatakan kemungkinan dengan might/may dan membicarakan teknologi masa depan

lessons.title: Plans, Arrangements and Decisions
lessons.summary: Membedakan will (keputusan spontan, tawaran, janji), be going to (niat/rencana), dan present continuous (janji temu yang sudah pasti).
objectives: Menggunakan will untuk keputusan spontan, tawaran, dan janji
Menggunakan be going to untuk rencana yang sudah diputuskan sebelumnya
Menggunakan present continuous untuk janji temu dengan waktu yang pasti
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Tiga cara membicarakan masa depan
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita cukup bilang *akan* atau *mau*. English has several future forms, and the choice depends on **when you made the decision** and **how fixed the plan is**.

| Form | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| will + V1 | keputusan spontan, tawaran, janji (instant decisions, offers, promises) | The phone's ringing. I'll get it. |
| be going to + V1 | niat/rencana yang sudah diputuskan sebelumnya (intentions) | I'm going to learn to code this year. |
| present continuous | janji temu/pengaturan yang sudah pasti (arrangements) | I'm meeting Dr. Salim at 10 tomorrow. |

### will: deciding now
Kita memakai **will** ketika keputusan dibuat **pada saat berbicara**. A: *We've run out of milk.* B: *Oh, I'll buy some on my way home.* Will is also used for **offers** (*I'll carry that bag for you*) and **promises** (*I won't tell anyone, I promise*). Bentuknya selalu **will/won't + V1**, tanpa *to*.

### be going to: decided before
**Going to** menunjukkan niat yang sudah ada **sebelum** berbicara. *I've decided — I'm going to sell my old laptop.* It is a personal plan; biasanya belum ada pengaturan dengan orang lain atau tiket yang dibeli. Remember the verb *be*: *She's going to start* (bukan ~~she going to start~~).

### Present continuous: in the diary
Present continuous for the future = an **arrangement**. Biasanya ada **waktu yang jelas** dan sering melibatkan **orang lain**, tiket, atau booking: *We're flying to Port Selwyn on Friday. Dina is having a party on Saturday.* If you can write it in your calendar, the present continuous is a good choice. Jangan pakai present simple untuk rencana pribadi: ~~I meet my boss tomorrow~~ → *I'm meeting my boss tomorrow.*

### going to atau present continuous?
Untuk rencana, kedua bentuk ini sering sama-sama benar: *I'm going to see / I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow.* The difference is small: going to focuses on the **intention**, the present continuous on the **arrangement**. Tetapi untuk **keputusan spontan** dan **tawaran**, pilih **will**: A: *This box is so heavy!* B: *I'll help you.*

### Ringkas
Ask yourself: Did I decide just now? → **will**. Did I decide before? → **going to**. Is it fixed with a time, a person, or a ticket? → **present continuous**.

lessons.title: Making Predictions
lessons.summary: Membuat prediksi dengan will (opini) dan be going to (bukti saat ini), serta memakai probably, definitely, dan I don't think ... will.
objectives: Membedakan prediksi berdasarkan opini (will) dan bukti saat ini (going to)
Menempatkan probably dan definitely dengan benar
Membuat prediksi negatif dengan I don't think ... will
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Membuat prediksi
A **prediction** is what we think will happen in the future. Dalam bahasa Inggris ada dua pilihan utama: **will** dan **be going to**. Keduanya bisa diterjemahkan *akan*, tetapi dasar prediksinya berbeda.

| Form | Dasar prediksi | Example |
|---|---|---|
| will + V1 | opini, keyakinan, pengalaman (opinion/belief) | I think electric cars will be cheaper in ten years. |
| be going to + V1 | bukti yang terlihat sekarang (present evidence) | Look at that queue! We're going to wait for hours. |

### will untuk opini
We often use will after **I think**, **I'm sure**, **I expect**, **I believe** and with adverbs like **probably** and **definitely**. Prediksi ini berasal dari pikiran atau pengalaman kita, bukan dari sesuatu yang kita lihat saat ini: *I'm sure you'll pass the test.* *Prices will probably go up next year.*

### going to untuk bukti
Kalau ada tanda yang jelas **sekarang** — awan gelap, jalan macet, baterai hampir habis — gunakan *going to*: *My battery is at 2%. My phone is going to die!* The event often feels close or almost certain, because we can see it coming.

### Posisi probably dan definitely
| Positive | Negative |
|---|---|
| It **will probably** rain. | It **probably won't** rain. |
| She'**ll definitely** come. | She **definitely won't** come. |

Perhatikan: dalam kalimat positif, adverb diletakkan **setelah will**; dalam kalimat negatif, **sebelum won't**. So *won't probably* is wrong.

### I don't think ... will
To make a negative opinion, English speakers usually say **I don't think + will**, not *I think + won't*. *I don't think it will be busy* lebih natural daripada *I think it won't be busy*. Jangan memakai dua negatif: ~~I don't think he won't come~~.

### Present simple bukan untuk prediksi
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering berkata *Besok hujan*. In English, a prediction needs a future form: *It will rain tomorrow* or *It's going to rain tomorrow*, not ~~It rains tomorrow~~.

### Tips
In everyday conversation the difference between will and going to for predictions is sometimes small. But when you can **see the evidence now**, going to is the safest choice, and with **I think / I'm sure / probably**, will is the natural choice.

sections.summary: Use **will** for predictions based on opinion (often with *I think, I'm sure, probably, definitely*) and **going to** for predictions based on evidence you can see now. Letakkan *probably/definitely* **setelah will** tetapi **sebelum won't**, dan gunakan **I don't think ... will** untuk prediksi negatif.

reviewCards.back: will: I think AI will change many jobs.
going to: Look at the sky! It's going to rain.
sebelum won't: It probably won't rain.

reviewCards.front: I think it won't be busy. → lebih natural?
reviewCards.back: I don't think it will be busy.
prakiraan (cuaca): The forecast says it'll be sunny.

questions.prompt: Be careful! The ladder is moving. You ___ fall!
questions.explanation: Ada bukti yang terlihat sekarang (tangganya bergoyang) → **be going to + V1**: *You are going to fall!* Remember: we need **are** and **to**, and *will* is never followed by *to*.
questions.misconception: Going to selalu memakai be (am/is/are) dan to.

questions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
acceptedAnswers: Next year prices probably won't go down
questions.explanation: Dalam kalimat negatif, **probably** diletakkan **sebelum won't**: *Prices probably won't go down next year.* Time expressions like *next year* can go at the beginning or the end.

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it sounds more natural.
questions.sentence: I think it won't be easy to find a cheap flight.
answers: I don't think it will be easy to find a cheap flight.
I do not think it will be easy to find a cheap flight.
I don't think it'll be easy to find a cheap flight.
I do not think it'll be easy to find a cheap flight.
questions.explanation: Penutur asli biasanya berkata **I don't think + will**: *I don't think it will be easy...* The negative moves to *think*, so *will* stays positive.

questions.topic: predictions with will and going to
questions.prompt: Which sentences are correct? Choose all the correct ones.
options: Prices will probably rise next year.
Our team won't probably win the final.
Look at the score! We're going to lose this match.
I'm sure you'll love the new phone.
I think it doesn't rain tomorrow.
She will definitely to pass the exam.
questions.explanation: Benar: *will probably rise*, *going to lose* (bukti: skornya), *I'm sure you'll love*. Salah: *won't probably* (→ probably won't), *doesn't rain tomorrow* (prediksi butuh will), *will definitely to pass* (tanpa to).

questions.topic: predictions with will and going to
questions.prompt: Drag the correct words into the gaps.
questions.text: Experts expect that by 2040 most new cars ___ be electric. Petrol cars will ___ disappear from city centres. But look at the traffic outside today — we ___ going to be late for work!
answers: will
probably
are
questions.explanation: Opini para ahli → **will** be electric. Adverb setelah will → *will **probably** disappear*. Bukti sekarang (macet) → *we **are** going to be late*.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence.
questions.sentence: I don't think Andra won't come to the party.
answers: I don't think Andra will come to the party.
I do not think Andra will come to the party.
I don't think Andra'll come to the party.
questions.explanation: Hanya boleh **satu negatif**. *I don't think* sudah negatif, jadi pakai **will**, bukan *won't*: *I don't think Andra will come to the party.*

lessons.title: When, As Soon As, Until: Future Time Clauses
lessons.summary: Memakai present simple setelah when, as soon as, before, after, dan until saat membicarakan masa depan.
objectives: Menggunakan present simple (bukan will) dalam klausa waktu untuk masa depan
Memahami arti when, as soon as, before, after, dan until
Menggabungkan dua kalimat dengan klausa waktu dan tanda koma yang tepat
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Klausa waktu untuk masa depan
A **time clause** starts with a word like **when, as soon as, before, after** or **until**. Saat kalimat membicarakan masa depan, klausa waktu memakai **present simple**, bukan *will*. Ini berbeda dengan bahasa Indonesia, di mana kita bisa berkata *ketika saya akan tiba*. In English: *when I arrive*, not ~~when I will arrive~~.

| Time clause (present simple) | Main clause (future) |
|---|---|
| When I **get** home, | I'll call you. |
| As soon as the film **ends**, | we're going to leave. |
| Before you **go** out, | close the windows. |

### Arti setiap konjungsi
| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| when | ketika/saat | When the shop opens, I'll buy a charger. |
| as soon as | segera setelah | I'll text you as soon as I land. |
| before | sebelum | Charge your phone before you leave. |
| after | setelah | After we eat, we'll watch the match. |
| until | sampai | I'll wait here until you come back. |

### Urutan dan koma
The time clause can come **first** or **second**. Kalau klausa waktu ada di **awal**, pakai **koma**: *When I finish, I'll help you.* If it comes second, we usually don't use a comma: *I'll help you when I finish.* Artinya sama.

### Main clause
The main clause can use **will**, **going to**, or an **imperative** (kalimat perintah): *Call me when you arrive.* Yang penting: **will tidak masuk ke klausa waktu**. Only the main clause shows the future.

### Present perfect di klausa waktu
Sometimes we use the present perfect to show that the first action will be **completely finished**: *I'll call you when I've finished my homework.* Artinya hampir sama dengan *when I finish*, tetapi lebih menekankan 'sudah selesai'. Both are correct.

### Hati-hati dengan until
*Until* berarti 'sampai'. Use it with a **positive** verb: *I'll wait until he comes* (bukan ~~until he doesn't come~~). And remember: *until* is about time, so *I'll wait until six o'clock* is also correct.

examples.en: I'll send you the photos as soon as I get home.
examples.id: Saya akan mengirimkan foto-fotonya segera setelah saya sampai di rumah.

examples.en: When the new phone comes out, I'm going to buy it.
examples.id: Ketika ponsel baru itu keluar, saya akan membelinya.
examples.note: Klausa waktu di awal → pakai koma.

examples.en: Please don't turn off the computer before the update finishes.
examples.id: Tolong jangan matikan komputer sebelum pembaruan selesai.
examples.note: before + present simple; main clause berupa imperative.

examples.en: We'll stay inside until the storm stops.
examples.id: Kita akan tetap di dalam sampai badai berhenti.

examples.en: After Nadia graduates, she's going to work abroad.
examples.id: Setelah Nadia lulus, dia akan bekerja di luar negeri.

vocabulary.example: Call me as soon as you hear any news.
Wait here until I come back.
I'll text you when the plane lands.
I need to charge my phone before I go out.
Turn off the lights when you leave.
We'll talk about it when I get back.

grammar.pattern: when / as soon as / before / after / until + present simple, + will / going to / imperative
grammar.example: As soon as I arrive, I'll call you.
grammar.note: Koma dipakai jika klausa waktu di awal kalimat.

grammar.pattern: Main clause + when / as soon as / before / after / until + present simple
grammar.example: I'll call you as soon as I arrive.
grammar.note: Tanpa koma jika klausa waktu di akhir.

grammar.pattern: when / after / as soon as + present perfect (optional)
grammar.example: I'll lend you the book when I've finished it.
grammar.note: Menekankan bahwa aksi pertama sudah selesai.

mistakes.wrong: I'll call you when I will arrive.
mistakes.right: I'll call you when I arrive.
mistakes.why: Setelah when (untuk masa depan) pakai present simple, bukan will.

mistakes.wrong: As soon as she will finish, we'll leave.
mistakes.right: As soon as she finishes, we'll leave.
mistakes.why: As soon as + present simple; ingat -es untuk she.

mistakes.wrong: Don't go out until it doesn't stop raining.
mistakes.right: Don't go out until it stops raining.
mistakes.why: Until dipakai dengan kata kerja positif.

mistakes.wrong: Before you leave turn off the computer.
mistakes.right: Before you leave, turn off the computer.
mistakes.why: Jika klausa waktu di awal, pakai koma.

sections.summary: After **when, as soon as, before, after** and **until**, use the **present simple** to talk about the future — never *will*. Masa depan cukup ditunjukkan di main clause (will, going to, atau imperative). Pakai koma jika klausa waktu berada di awal kalimat.

reviewCards.back: arrive — present simple, bukan will arrive
segera setelah: I'll text you as soon as I land.
Positif: Wait until it stops raining.

reviewCards.front: Kapan pakai koma dengan klausa waktu?
reviewCards.back: Saat klausa waktu di awal: When I finish, I'll help you.
Boleh, untuk menekankan selesai: I'll call you when I've finished.

questions.prompt: Complete with the correct form of the verbs in brackets.
questions.text: When Raka ___ (finish) his course next year, he ___ (look) for a job in Port Selwyn.
answers: finishes
has finished
's finished
will look
'll look
is going to look
's going to look
questions.explanation: Klausa waktu dengan *when* memakai **present simple**: *finishes* (bukan *will finish*). The main clause shows the future: **will look** or **is going to look**.
questions.misconception: Banyak pelajar menulis 'when he will finish' karena dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bisa berkata 'ketika dia akan selesai'.

questions.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order to make a sentence.
acceptedAnswers: Please make sure you turn off all the computers before you leave the office.
questions.explanation: Klausa waktu *Before you leave the office* memakai present simple dan diikuti koma karena berada di awal. The main clause is an imperative: *please make sure...*

questions.prompt: Listen and type the sentence you hear.
questions.text: We'll stay inside until the storm stops.
questions.explanation: Kalimatnya: *We'll stay inside until the storm stops.* Notice that *until* is followed by the present simple **stops**, not *will stop*.

questions.prompt: Find the incorrect part of the sentence.
questions.explanation: Setelah **as soon as** untuk masa depan, gunakan present simple: *as soon as the plane **lands***. Only the main clause (*I'll call you*) uses will.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option for each gap.
questions.text: We ___ dinner until Dad gets home from work tonight. As soon as he ___, we'll start eating.
questions.explanation: Main clause tentang malam ini → **won't have**. Klausa *as soon as* untuk masa depan → present simple **arrives**, bukan *will arrive*.

questions.prompt: Combine the two sentences into one.
questions.sentence: First I'll finish this report. Then I'll go home.
questions.cue: Use 'after'. Begin with: I'll go home ...
answers: I'll go home after I finish this report.
I will go home after I finish this report.
I'll go home after I've finished this report.
I will go home after I have finished this report.
I'll go home after I have finished this report.
I will go home after I've finished this report.
questions.explanation: Setelah **after** pakai present simple (*I finish*) atau present perfect (*I've finished*), bukan *will finish*: *I'll go home after I finish this report.*

lessons.title: Might and May for Possibility
lessons.summary: Menyatakan kemungkinan di masa depan dengan might/may dan membandingkan tingkat keyakinan (will, probably, might, won't).
objectives: Menggunakan might/may + V1 untuk kemungkinan di masa depan
Membentuk kalimat negatif might not / may not
Membedakan maybe dan may be serta memilih kata sesuai tingkat keyakinan
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### might dan may = mungkin
We use **might** or **may** + V1 to say that something is **possible** but not certain. Dalam bahasa Indonesia artinya *mungkin* atau *bisa jadi*. *It might rain this afternoon. I may be late tonight.* Kita memakainya ketika kita belum memutuskan atau belum tahu pasti.

### Bentuk
| Positive | Negative |
|---|---|
| I might / may go. | I might not / may not go. |
| She might / may be busy. | She might not / may not be busy. |

Seperti modal lain (*can, will, should*): tidak ada **-s** untuk he/she/it, tidak ada **to**, dan kata kerja setelahnya selalu **V1**. *He might come* (bukan ~~he mights come~~ / ~~he might to come~~ / ~~he might coming~~). The negative is usually not contracted: say *might not* and *may not*.

### Seberapa yakin?
| Certainty | Example |
|---|---|
| 100% | It **will** rain. / It's **definitely** going to rain. |
| ±80% | It'll **probably** rain. |
| ±50% | It **might / may** rain. |
| ±20% | It **probably won't** rain. |
| 0% | It **won't** rain. |

The percentages are only a guide, tetapi tabel ini membantu kamu memilih kata yang tepat untuk tingkat keyakinanmu.

### might vs may
Dalam konteks kemungkinan, *might* dan *may* hampir sama artinya. *May* sounds a little more formal and is common in news and official messages: *Flights may be delayed because of the storm.* *Might* is very common in everyday conversation: *I might watch a film tonight.*

### maybe vs may be
**Maybe** (satu kata) adalah adverb = *mungkin*, biasanya di awal kalimat: *Maybe I'll stay at home.* **May be** (dua kata) adalah modal + verb *be*: *The shop may be closed.* Jangan tertukar! A quick test: if you can replace it with *perhaps*, write **maybe**.

### Pertanyaan
We don't usually ask questions with *might/may* for possibility. Instead, ask: *Do you think it will rain?* atau *Are you going to come?* The answer can use might: *I'm not sure. I might.*

mistakes.wrong: He mights come later.
mistakes.right: He might come later.
mistakes.why: Modal tidak pernah mendapat -s.

mistakes.wrong: We might to visit the museum.
mistakes.right: We might visit the museum.
mistakes.why: Setelah might/may langsung V1, tanpa to.

mistakes.wrong: May be I'll stay at home tonight.
mistakes.right: Maybe I'll stay at home tonight.
mistakes.why: Sebagai adverb (= perhaps), maybe ditulis satu kata.

mistakes.right: Do you think you'll come to the party?
mistakes.why: Untuk menanyakan kemungkinan, biasanya pakai Do you think ... will ...? atau Are you going to ...?

sections.summary: **Might** and **may** + V1 express possibility (*mungkin*): *It might rain.* Bentuk negatifnya *might not / may not*; tidak ada -s, tidak ada to. *Maybe* (satu kata) = perhaps, sedangkan *may be* = modal + be. Choose will, probably, might, or won't according to how certain you are.

reviewCards.back: V1 tanpa to: It might rain.
might not: I might not go.
Maybe = perhaps (adverb). May be = modal + be: It may be closed.
will > will probably > might/may > probably won't > won't
may — sering di pengumuman resmi.

questions.prompt: Take an umbrella. It ___ rain later — the forecast isn't sure.
questions.explanation: **might + V1** untuk kemungkinan: *It might rain later.* Modal tidak memakai *to*, tidak mendapat *-s*, dan tidak memakai *is*.
questions.misconception: Might adalah modal seperti can dan will: langsung diikuti V1.

questions.prompt: Complete with might not or may not + the verb in brackets.
questions.text: Bayu isn't feeling well, so he ___ (come) to football practice tonight. We aren't sure yet.
answers: might not come
may not come
mightn't come
questions.explanation: Belum pasti dan negatif → **might not come** / **may not come**. The verb after the modal is always V1 (*come*).

questions.prompt: Translate into Indonesian.
questions.source: The new app might not be ready until next month.
answers: Aplikasi baru itu mungkin tidak akan siap sampai bulan depan.
Aplikasi baru itu mungkin belum siap sampai bulan depan.
Aplikasi baru itu mungkin tidak siap sampai bulan depan.
Aplikasi yang baru itu mungkin belum siap sampai bulan depan.
Aplikasi yang baru itu mungkin tidak akan siap sampai bulan depan.
Aplikasi baru itu mungkin baru siap bulan depan.
Aplikasi baru itu mungkin belum akan siap sampai bulan depan.
questions.explanation: *might not be ready* = **mungkin tidak/belum siap**; *until next month* = **sampai bulan depan**. Perhatikan bahwa *might not* menunjukkan ketidakpastian, not a definite fact.

questions.prompt: Rewrite with may + verb. Write only the missing words (two words). 'Perhaps the shop is closed today.' → The shop ___ closed today.
answers: may be
questions.explanation: *Perhaps ... is* → **may be** (modal *may* + verb *be*), ditulis dua kata: *The shop may be closed today.* *Maybe* (one word) is an adverb and cannot replace the verb.

questions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: Pola negatif: **subject + may not + V1**: *We may not have enough time to visit the museum.* *Not* comes directly after *may*.

questions.explanation: Gilang belum memutuskan → **might + V1**: *I might go with my cousin.* The other options use the wrong verb form after *might*.

lessons.title: Technology and the Future
lessons.summary: Membicarakan teknologi masa depan dengan kosakata yang tepat dan menggabungkan semua bentuk future yang telah dipelajari.
objectives: Menggunakan kosakata teknologi seperti device, replace, develop, update, dan driverless
Menggabungkan will, going to, present continuous, might/may, dan time clauses
Menulis paragraf pendek berisi prediksi tentang teknologi
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Membicarakan teknologi masa depan
In this lesson you will put all the future forms together to talk about **technology**. Saat berdiskusi tentang masa depan, kita perlu kosakata yang tepat **dan** cara menunjukkan seberapa yakin kita.

### Kosakata inti
| Word / phrase | Meaning | Collocation |
|---|---|---|
| device | perangkat | a smart device, a mobile device |
| artificial intelligence (AI) | kecerdasan buatan | use AI, AI tools |
| driverless | tanpa sopir | a driverless car |
| replace | menggantikan | replace workers, replace paper tickets |
| develop | mengembangkan | develop an app, develop new technology |
| update | memperbarui | update software, update an app |
| battery | baterai | charge the battery, the battery runs out |

### Ringkasan bentuk future
| Situation | Form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| opinion prediction | will (+ probably/definitely) | AI will probably change many jobs. |
| evidence now | going to | My laptop is making a strange noise. It's going to break! |
| plan / intention | going to | I'm going to learn to code. |
| fixed arrangement | present continuous | We're launching the new app on 1 March. |
| possibility | might / may | Driverless buses might appear in our city. |
| time clause | when / as soon as + present simple | When the update finishes, restart your phone. |

### Mengekspresikan pendapat tentang masa depan
Useful phrases: *In the future, ...*, *In ten years' time, ...*, *I expect (that) ...*, *I doubt (that) ... will ...*, *There's a good chance that ...* Kata **doubt** berarti 'ragu', jadi *I doubt robots will cook our dinner* artinya kamu tidak yakin hal itu akan terjadi. *There's a good chance* means something is quite likely.

### Menulis prediksi yang baik
A good paragraph about the future **mixes certainty levels**. Jangan hanya memakai *will* di setiap kalimat. Example: *I think phones will probably become even thinner. Some people might wear them as glasses. However, I don't think robots will replace teachers, because students need real human contact.* Paragraf ini memakai *will probably*, *might*, dan *I don't think ... will* — sehingga terdengar lebih alami dan lebih jujur.

### Tips
Give a **reason** for your prediction with *because* or *so*: *Online shopping will grow because it's fast and easy.* Alasan membuat pendapatmu lebih meyakinkan.

sections.summary: To talk about the future of technology, combine **will/probably** (opinion), **going to** (evidence or plans), **present continuous** (arrangements), **might/may** (possibility) and **time clauses + present simple**. Gunakan kosakata seperti *device, replace, develop, update, driverless*, dan beri alasan untuk setiap prediksi.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word. My phone's ___ is almost empty, so I need to charge it.
questions.explanation: Yang perlu di-*charge* (diisi daya) adalah **battery**. A screen shows pictures, and an update is new software.

questions.prompt: Match each word with its definition.

pairs.right: a small machine or tool, such as a phone or tablet
to take the place of something or someone
to create something new and make it better over time
able to move without a person controlling it
to install the newest version of software

questions.explanation: device = perangkat; replace = menggantikan; develop = mengembangkan; driverless = tanpa sopir; update = memperbarui (software).

questions.prompt: How will technology change your daily life in the next 20 years? Write a paragraph of 80–120 words.
questions.instructions: Use will (with probably/definitely), might or may, I don't think ... will, and at least one time clause (when / as soon as / before / after / until). Give reasons with because or so.
questions.explanation: Paragraf yang baik mencampur tingkat keyakinan (will probably, might, I don't think ... will) dan memberi alasan. Check that every time clause uses the present simple, not will.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word. Some people worry that robots will ___ human workers in factories.
questions.explanation: **Replace** = menggantikan. Orang khawatir robot akan mengambil tempat pekerja manusia. *Repair* (memperbaiki), *remind* (mengingatkan) and *receive* (menerima) do not make sense here.

questions.prompt: Drag the correct words into the gaps.
questions.text: Scientists are ___ a new kind of battery. When it ___ ready, phones will charge in five minutes. However, it ___ not be cheap at first — nobody knows yet.
answers: developing
is
might
questions.explanation: *are **developing*** = sedang mengembangkan. Klausa waktu *When it **is** ready* memakai present simple. *Nobody knows yet* → kemungkinan → *it **might** not be cheap*.

questions.prompt: Translate into English.
questions.source: Saya ragu robot akan menggantikan guru.
answers: I doubt robots will replace teachers.
I doubt that robots will replace teachers.
I doubt robots are going to replace teachers.
I doubt that robots are going to replace teachers.
I doubt robots will replace the teachers.
I doubt that robots will replace the teachers.
I doubt robots'll replace teachers.
questions.explanation: *Saya ragu ... akan* = **I doubt (that) ... will**; *menggantikan* = **replace**. Because *doubt* is already negative, we use **will**, not *won't*.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Which sentence describes a fixed arrangement?
options: I'm flying to Port Selwyn at 6:15 on Monday — here's my ticket.
I think I'll fly to Port Selwyn one day.
It might be sunny in Port Selwyn.
I'll probably fly there next year.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Waktu pasti dan tiket sudah ada → arrangement → **present continuous**: *I'm flying ... at 6:15 on Monday.* The other sentences are opinions or possibilities.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
unitTestQuestions.text: Please wait here until the doctor ___ (call) your name.
answers: calls
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Setelah **until** untuk masa depan → present simple: *until the doctor **calls** your name*. Jangan pakai *will call*.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Choose the correct option for each gap.
unitTestQuestions.text: A: Have you decided what to do after university? B: Yes, I ___ a master's degree in Port Selwyn. A: That's great! I'm sure you ___ it.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Rencana yang sudah diputuskan (*Have you decided...? Yes*) → **am going to do**. Prediksi opini setelah *I'm sure* → **will love**.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Find the incorrect part of the sentence.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Klausa waktu memakai present simple: *when she **gets** to the station*. *Will* hanya ada di main clause (*will call you*).

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with the same meaning.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: Perhaps Kevin will join us for lunch.
answers: Kevin might join us for lunch.
Kevin may join us for lunch.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Perhaps ... will* = kemungkinan → **might + V1**: *Kevin might join us for lunch.*

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
acceptedAnswers: On Friday I'm having lunch with my old classmates
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Arrangement dengan teman dan waktu pasti → present continuous: *I'm having lunch with my old classmates on Friday.*

dialogue.speaker: Fajar
dialogue.text: I can't open the file you sent. My laptop is too old.

options: Don't worry. I'll send it again in a different format.
Don't worry. I send it again in a different format.
Don't worry. I sent it again tomorrow.
Don't worry. I'll sending it again in a different format.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Wulan memutuskan saat itu juga → **will + V1**: *I'll send it again.* Present simple and past simple do not express an instant decision about the future.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Choose the best word. The weather ___ says it will be sunny all weekend.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **Weather forecast** = prakiraan cuaca. *Invention* (penemuan), *schedule* (jadwal), and *device* (perangkat) do not collocate with *weather* here.
